title: Transaction envelope followed by two zero bytes must be refused by the transaction parser
caps_note: An XDR decoding rule (a value is the whole input: stellar-core refuses an envelope with bytes after it), not a CAP.
why: A complete 136-byte TransactionEnvelope with two zero bytes after it is not a TransactionEnvelope. 136 is 1 mod 3, so in base64 the extra bytes share the final 4-character quantum with the envelope's last byte: a parser that checks consumption by counting base64 characters instead of decoded bytes accepts the input, and two different strings then parse to the same transaction.

known_divergences.detail: Executed on v0.7.1, v0.7.2, v0.7.3, v0.8.0 and v0.9.0: txnbuild.TransactionFromXDR, through xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64, parses the envelope and ignores the two zero bytes after it; the same SDK refuses three extra bytes (member three-bytes-next-quantum). Fix proposed in pull request #6041, not merged.

notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/xdr-strict/api-transaction-parse-trailing-bytes.two-bytes-in-final-quantum.json. Origin: go-stellar-sdk#6039. The envelope is hand-encoded: ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX, an ed25519 source, fee 100, sequence 1, PRECOND_NONE, MEMO_TEXT "xcc", one native payment of 1 XLM, no signatures; 136 bytes. xdr_hex is that envelope followed by two zero bytes. The driver passes the bytes to the SDK the way an application receives an envelope (base64 for go-stellar-sdk's txnbuild.TransactionFromXDR). Expected values were computed from the XDR definitions and the rule cited under related, with an independent encoder; no SDK output was used.
